You'll find our 50cl bottles in open markets, neighbourhood supermarkets and at our stands in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In January we're launching a 1L family bottle. Families tell us they buy two or three 50cl bottles at a time for the house, so one bigger bottle saves them money and a trip.

Who buys it
Mostly parents aged 25 to 44 who shop for the whole house. They compare prices, and they choose in a few seconds at a shelf or a cooler, often with children asking for something else.

What we know so far
The drink inside is the same zobo and ginger, so taste isn't the problem.
On a shelf, the 1L bottle looks like a bigger copy of the 50cl one, so people miss that it's new.
Shops put it on the bottom shelf because it's tall, which hides the label.

What we can change
The label, the cap colour and the neck tag. We can't change the bottle mould this year. | Problem statement | 223 / 2,000 | On a crowded shelf, our 1L bottle doesn't look new and doesn't look like it's for sharing. We want packaging ideas that make a parent notice it, see straight away that it's the family size, and still know it's Orchid Foods. | Deliverables | 3 of 3 | One packaging idea for the 1L bottle: the label, the cap colour or the neck tag, described in words. | Where on the shelf a parent would notice it first, and why that makes them pick it up. | One sentence on the family you pictured while you wrote it. | Up to 3 things every submission must include. | Success criteria | 4 of 5 | Easy to spot on a crowded shelf | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Says family size at a glance | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Still looks like Orchid Foods | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Works on our current bottle, with no new mould | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Add criterion | Up to 5. You'll find our 50cl bottles in open markets, neighbourhood supermarkets and at our stands in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In January we're launching a 1L family bottle. Families tell us they buy two or three 50cl bottles at a time for the house, so one bigger bottle saves them money and a trip.

Who buys it
Mostly parents aged 25 to 44 who shop for the whole house. They compare prices, and they choose in a few seconds at a shelf or a cooler, often with children asking for something else.

What we know so far
The drink inside is the same zobo and ginger, so taste isn't the problem.
On a shelf, the 1L bottle looks like a bigger copy of the 50cl one, so people miss that it's new.
Shops put it on the bottom shelf because it's tall, which hides the label.

What we can change
The label, the cap colour and the neck tag. We can't change the bottle mould this year. | Problem statement | 223 / 2,000 | On a crowded shelf, our 1L bottle doesn't look new and doesn't look like it's for sharing. We want packaging ideas that make a parent notice it, see straight away that it's the family size, and still know it's Orchid Foods. | Deliverables | 3 of 3 | One packaging idea for the 1L bottle: the label, the cap colour or the neck tag, described in words. | Where on the shelf a parent would notice it first, and why that makes them pick it up. | One sentence on the family you pictured while you wrote it. | Up to 3 things every submission must include. | Success criteria | 4 of 5 | Easy to spot on a crowded shelf | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Says family size at a glance | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Still looks like Orchid Foods | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Works on our current bottle, with no new mould | Importance | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | Add criterion | Up to 5. To accept images, PDFs and video links, choose Advanced in Type. | Back | Continue | How your brief is used | Contributors read it before they write, so put what they need to know in the overview.

You'll find our 50cl bottles in open markets, neighbourhood supermarkets and at our stands in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In January we're launching a 1L family bottle. Families tell us they buy two or three 50cl bottles at a time for the house, so one bigger bottle saves them money and a trip.

Who buys it
Mostly parents aged 25 to 44 who shop for the whole house. They compare prices, and they choose in a few seconds at a shelf or a cooler, often with children asking for something else.

What we know so far
The drink inside is the same zobo and ginger, so taste isn't the problem.
On a shelf, the 1L bottle looks like a bigger copy of the 50cl one, so people miss that it's new.
Shops put it on the bottom shelf because it's tall, which hides the label.

What we can change
The label, the cap colour and the neck tag. We can't change the bottle mould this year. | The problem | On a crowded shelf, our 1L bottle doesn't look new and doesn't look like it's for sharing. We want packaging ideas that make a parent notice it, see straight away that it's the family size, and still know it's Orchid Foods. | What you’ll deliver | •  One packaging idea for the 1L bottle: the label, the cap colour or the neck tag, described in words. | •  Where on the shelf a parent would notice it first, and why that makes them pick it up. | •  One sentence on the family you pictured while you wrote it. | What good looks like | •  Easy to spot on a crowded shelf. | •  Says family size at a glance. | •  Still looks like Orchid Foods. | •  Works on our current bottle, with no new mould. | Back | Continue

You'll find our 50cl bottles in open markets, neighbourhood supermarkets and at our stands in Lagos, Ogun and Oyo.

In January we're launching a 1L family bottle. Families tell us they buy two or three 50cl bottles at a time for the house, so one bigger bottle saves them money and a trip.

Who buys it
Mostly parents aged 25 to 44 who shop for the whole house. They compare prices, and they choose in a few seconds at a shelf or a cooler, often with children asking for something else.

What we know so far
The drink inside is the same zobo and ginger, so taste isn't the problem.
On a shelf, the 1L bottle looks like a bigger copy of the 50cl one, so people miss that it's new.
Shops put it on the bottom shelf because it's tall, which hides the label.

What we can change
The label, the cap colour and the neck tag. We can't change the bottle mould this year. | The problem | On a crowded shelf, our 1L bottle doesn't look new and doesn't look like it's for sharing. We want packaging ideas that make a parent notice it, see straight away that it's the family size, and still know it's Orchid Foods. | What you’ll deliver | •  One packaging idea for the 1L bottle: the label, the cap colour or the neck tag, described in words. | •  Where on the shelf a parent would notice it first, and why that makes them pick it up. | •  One sentence on the family you pictured while you wrote it. | What good looks like | •  Easy to spot on a crowded shelf. | •  Says family size at a glance. | •  Still looks like Orchid Foods. | •  Works on our current bottle, with no new mould. | Back | Continue

9:41 | Shortlist | Not considering | 1 of 15 · Ifeoma Nwosu, 6 Oct | Zobolicious, loud and local | Zobo, but louder. Made here, sold here, and it says so on the can. Long for a name, but it sounds like a market call.

Picture the seller at Balogun with a cooler of cold cans: "Zobolicious! Loud and local!" It is easy to shout, easy to remember, and it tells you what is inside before you read the label.

On the shelf the word does the work. Put it in bold on a deep red can with a ginger stripe, and the "loud" part becomes the design: big type, no pictures needed.

Why it fits the brief: it keeps zobo in the name, it says the drink is from here, and it has energy without sounding like a copy of a soft drink.

One risk: it is long for a small can. "Zobo-licious" with the hyphen may read faster at a glance. | Not considering | Shortlist | Pass | Swipe right to shortlist, left to pass

desktop/01-sign-in.description: Row 1 · Sign in for businesses. Copy from apps/brand/src/routes/_auth (login, signup, verify-email, forgot-password). Sign in opens Home; Forgot? opens the reset form; Create business opens Check your email. 390 Create business has no Check your email copy yet (same as 1440). Send reset link and Resend email have no next screen (deliberate dead ends).

desktop/02-home-and-challenges.title: Row 1 · Business home and challenges
desktop/02-home-and-challenges.description:
Experimental. White canvas, light sidebar with Exp icons, the official iQLY for Business wordmark and a workspace switcher: clearly the business product, not the contributor app.
Home (Grey layout): Waiting on you (C6 changes, P5 change, 19 claims to confirm on A1), challenge escrow with a per-challenge breakdown and round actions next to live polls, one figure strip, recent submissions with quality score. Fix and resubmit opens the edit form directly (C6 in row 2, P5 in Polls row 3); Review claims opens the A1 queue; escrow rows open C2, C1 and C6.
Challenges: tabs by status. Live detail: submissions, judging, and Publish winners as in code (publish-panel.tsx): disabled until judging ends on 23 Oct, then a confirm step lists each winner and amount before ₦1,500,000 leaves escrow.
Data: illustrative Orchid Foods set. Escrow C2 ₦3,000,000 + C1 ₦1,500,000 + C6 ₦700,000 = ₦5,200,000. Paid to winners ₦2,000,000 + ₦4,000,000 = ₦6,000,000. Votes 214 + 158 = 372. A1: 431 confirmed + 19 to confirm + 7 need info + 5 rejected = 462.
Dead ends on purpose: closed rows (C4, C5), Export, View public page, B03 submission rows and tabs, Request a challenge (assisted requests start from ₦200,000), Verification, Profile, the escrow eye toggle and the top bar (search, notifications, help, avatar, workspace switcher). Home is drawn once; it does not change after a task.

desktop/02-home-and-challenges.title: Row 2 · Payments, C3 in review, C6 fix and resubmit
desktop/02-home-and-challenges.description:
Payments: money in (pools, fees, activation budgets) and money out (winners, activation payouts) in one ledger. Kobo on totals and ledger rows, whole naira elsewhere. Ledger rows and Download statement are not linked.
C3 in review: where Continue to Paystack lands at the end of the C3 builder. ₦800,000 pool + 20% fee ₦160,000 = ₦960,000; the Paystack fee is shown on the Paystack receipt. Paystack checkout is off-site and not drawn. Withdraw opens the paid, withdrawn review step (Targeting row 1), which resubmits without a second payment. Back goes to Challenges after paying for C3.
C6 fix and resubmit: the two must-change notes sit beside their fields, and the audience is edited to University students to match the brief (What you sent keeps the original Students). Resubmit lands on C6 in review after changes, whose Withdraw returns to the edit; its back link and sidebar open Challenges after resubmitting C6. The ₦700,000 pool stays in escrow throughout.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 1 · New challenge: all ten steps, then withdrawn
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description:
Proposal on the shipped builder’s steps: Type, Basics, Brief, Cover, Survey, Audience (hidden in the shipped builder), Reward, Timeline, Brand visibility (Anonymity in the shipped builder), Review and fund. Brief is the big step: overview (up to 5,000 characters), problem statement (up to 2,000), up to 3 deliverables and up to 5 success criteria with importance 1 to 5. Cover is optional (empty, then uploaded); contributors see it on the challenge card on Discover and at the top of the brief. Audience adds University and Poll answers to the shipped filters; the second Audience frame is Advanced targeting.
C3 Packaging ideas: Standard, ₦800,000, cap 80 submissions, 14 days open then 7 days judging, Top N split with 3 winners (60 / 30 / 10: ₦480,000, ₦240,000, ₦80,000). Fee 20% ₦160,000, total ₦960,000. Review and fund keeps Continue to Paystack at the footer right. Finished steps on the rail and in the strip open their step. Save and exit sits next to the Preview switch on every step and goes to Challenges, where the draft waits. Collapse steps sits at the top of the rail, in the same spot as Expand steps.
Withdrawn (already paid): Tier is fixed at payment and the pool is shown as paid. Back, Audience Edit and Edit split open paid copies of the Audience and Reward steps (pool locked, Paid 10 Oct box) whose buttons return to the review. Resubmit for review needs no second payment.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 2 · From poll P3, then fund
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description:
Proposal. Start a challenge from an ended poll (P3) opens the builder with the poll answer already targeted (C2, Advanced, ₦3,000,000, 10 winners). Review and fund: summary, declaration and the payment summary: ₦3,000,000 pool + 20% fee ₦600,000 = ₦3,600,000, Paystack fee added at checkout. Continue to Paystack lands on the C2 in review detail (row 1 of Home and challenges). Withdrawn (already paid) resubmits without a second payment; its Back and Edit links open paid copies of the Audience and Reward steps.
C2’s Basics to Survey and Timeline to Brand visibility are not drawn; those finished steps on its rail and strip are not linked.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 3 · No tag polls yet, and from poll P1
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description: The no tag polls frame is the state for a business that hasn’t run a tag poll yet; Create a poll opens New poll for that draft, with Back to draft.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 4 · New challenge help, collapsed steps and a long title
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description:
Help links open a popover under the link: Which tier fits? (Type), How your brief is used (Brief), How targeting works (Audience), How the money works (Reward, Review and fund). The close button and the link both go back, and the popover follows its link when the steps are collapsed.
Brief with the steps collapsed: the rail becomes a strip under the title and the brief takes the full width.
Basics with a 200-character title: the title stops at 640 px and the current crumb at 320 px, each ending with an ellipsis, so the save status and Save and exit stay clear of it. The title field keeps one line.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 5 · New challenge previews, desktop
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description: Preview on Desktop in step order from Basics to Review: the iqly.net brief page in a browser, scaled to fit, filling in as the steps are done. Until a cover is added, the brief shows the default cover. Each sits under its step in row 1.

desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.title: Row 6 · New challenge previews, mobile
desktop/03-builder-and-targeting.description: Preview on Mobile in step order: the contributor app’s brief in a phone at actual size, drawn full length so the whole brief can be read. Each sits under its step in row 1.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 1 · Poll library
desktop/04-polls.description:
Proposal, not in code. Polls live in the business account so every result stays reachable. Two types from the owner’s draft: answers saved to contributor profiles as tags (usable for targeting) or one-off (results only). Every poll goes through iQLY review first (Draft, In review, Live, Ended, or Action needed).
Data: illustrative Orchid Foods polls P1 to P6. P1 matches the contributor screens (214 votes, 45 / 33 / 22). 372 = 214 + 158. 1,180 tags from P3; after P1 ends, 1,394 tags across two polls (some people hold tags from both).
Empty: the first visit explains both types before the first poll. The library after ending P1 early, after resubmitting P5 and after sending P6 is where those flows return (back links and sidebar).
Dead ends on purpose: P2 View results (no P2 results frame) and the tabs.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 2 · Create a poll (tags and one-off)
desktop/04-polls.description:
Proposal. Five rail steps: Type (tags or one-off), Question and options (2 to 4, each option shows the tag it creates), Cover, Audience and timing, Review. Cover is optional: the empty drop zone, then the uploaded photo, which contributors see at the top of the poll and on its card in Quick polls. Drafts save as you go and the status beside the title says when; Save and exit goes to the Polls library with the draft kept. Collapse steps, at the top of the rail, folds the rail into a strip under the title and the form takes the full width; Expand steps, in the same spot, brings it back (row 5 shows it collapsed). The tag path re-enacts how P4 was made (8 to 9 Oct).
One-off path (P6 draft): Type with One-off selected, Question, Cover, Audience and timing, Review, then in review. Back and Edit on the one-off path return to the one-off steps. Finished steps on the rail and in the strip open their step. Withdraw on the in-review frame returns to the question step.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 3 · Review, results, end early, resubmit
desktop/04-polls.description:
Proposal. In review (info banner, status timeline, Withdraw), action needed (flagged options and one must-change note), live results with End poll early, ended with Start a challenge from this poll (P3), ended early (P1) with its own start into Targeting row 3 (the P1 tags are now targetable), edit after changes and in review after changes (P5).
Numbers: P1 96 + 71 + 47 = 214 (45 / 33 / 22). P3 342 + 451 + 268 + 119 = 1,180 (29 / 38 / 23 / 10). Age split is illustrative: 101 + 71 + 30 + 12 = 214. Bars are drawn at the exact share of the track.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 4 · End poll early (dialog)
desktop/04-polls.description: Opens over Live results, which show through a 40% scrim. End poll (destructive) ends the poll and lands on Ended early; Keep it running, the close button or a click on the dimmed page closes it. Plain click to confirm, as in the shipped confirm dialogs.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 5 · New poll help and collapsed steps
desktop/04-polls.description:
Help links open a popover under the link: How tags work (Type and Question), How one-off polls work, Where it shows, What happens next. The close button and the link both go back. The popover follows its link when the steps are collapsed.
Question with the steps collapsed: the rail becomes a strip under the title (Expand steps, then the numbered steps with the current one named) and the form fills the width. Finished step numbers open their step.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 6 · New poll previews, tags
desktop/04-polls.description: Every step has the Edit and Preview switch in the same place; on Type, Preview is disabled until there is a question. Preview hides the rail and form and shows a full-width stage: Mobile is the contributor app in a phone at actual size, Desktop the iqly.net page in a browser, scaled to fit. In step order: Question, Cover (empty, then uploaded), Audience and timing, Review. Until a cover is added, the poll shows the default cover.

desktop/04-polls.title: Row 7 · New poll previews, one-off
desktop/04-polls.description: The same previews for the one-off poll (P6 draft) in step order: Question, Cover, Audience and timing, Review, Mobile then Desktop for each.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 1 · Activations for businesses
desktop/05-activations.description: Claims list is full width with a Status filter (default To confirm). Each claim opens its own page (Activations › activation › contributor) with the recording in full and Confirm, Ask for info and Reject under it; Confirm opens the next claim with a toast.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 2 · New activation steps, devices menu, help and collapsed steps
desktop/05-activations.description: Four rail steps: Task (row 1), Cover (empty, then uploaded; contributors see it at the top of the activation), Reward and spots, Review and pay, each with Save and exit and the Edit and Preview switch. How the money works opens under its link on Review and pay. The first frame is Task with the steps collapsed into the strip under the title. Every step’s device chip opens its Devices menu in place, and each device toggles with a click; the devices open frame and the collapsed frame are reference frames outside the click-through. Task’s Continue goes to the saved cover; Cover · empty is what Remove shows. Steps can carry an optional help line (Help for this step), shown under the step in Review, the previews and on iqly.net. Reward and spots asks how much to fund now: Every spot, or Part now with an amount (₦100,000 covers 100 of 200 spots). The choice sets the A2 funding variables that Review and pay, How the money works, the in-review page and every Activations list read; the part-now reference in row 4 shows Part now picked.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 3 · New activation previews
desktop/05-activations.description: Mobile and Desktop previews in step order: Task, Cover (empty, then uploaded), Reward and spots, Review and pay. Until a cover is added, the activation shows the default cover. Steps 2 to 5 show their help lines.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 4 · Empty new activation and steps opened from Review
desktop/05-activations.description: New activation, on every Activations list, opens the empty Task: blank fields, one empty step on All devices, no confirmation picked, and Preview and Continue disabled until there is something to show. How steps work opens its help in place. Edit and the rail on Review and pay open Task, Cover and Reward from review: every other step is Done and linked, and the footer has only Save and go to Review. Remove on Cover from review opens Cover · empty from review. Help popovers close back to the step they were opened from. Also in this row: the after funding list with the Live row menu open, and Reward and spots with Part now picked (reference).

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 5 · Withdraw to Draft, cancel or add money while in review
desktop/05-activations.description:
More on the activation in review opens its menu: Withdraw to Draft and Cancel activation, with Add money above them when only part of the spots is funded. Withdraw to Draft opens a dialog (Keep in review, the close button and the scrim go back); Withdraw sets A2 back to Draft and opens Activations with a toast: the money stays held in escrow, so resubmitting costs nothing. Cancel activation opens a dialog (Keep it goes back); Cancel activation marks A2 Cancelled, sends the money held to iQLY credit and opens Activations with a toast. Add money opens a dialog with the amount that covers every spot, paid with Paystack or, when there is enough, iQLY credit; it opens the in-review page with a toast. The part-now reference shows the menu and the page when only part is funded.
Money follows the path (Prototype state variables read by Payments, Home and every Activations list): after paying, Held in escrow ₦5,434,500.00 (₦5,334,500.00 with Part now), “3 challenges and 2 activations”, Paid in ₦13,995,000.00 (₦13,895,000.00) and an In escrow ledger row, which stays while the activation is withdrawn to Draft; after a cancel, escrow ₦5,234,500.00, iQLY credit ₦200,000.00 (₦100,000.00) and the ledger row shows Refunded, To iQLY credit. Paying again with Paystack is a second payment, so Paid in grows; paying from iQLY credit moves credit into escrow and leaves Paid in as it is. Add money gets its own ledger row (Added to the activation budget, Paid in +₦100,000.00 or From iQLY credit ₦100,000.00), Refunded after a cancel. Every Paid in movement has its own + row, so the + rows add up to Paid in; older rows move to page 2 so page 1 keeps 8 rows, and the footer counts them (of 12, 13 or 14). The prototype keeps the figures right for up to two payments, one Add money and two cancels (21 paths checked by script). Toasts close after 4 seconds. The Payments reference (mode After cancel) shows the page after a cancel.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 6 · From the Activations list, and a cancelled activation
desktop/05-activations.description:
More on the In review row of the Activations list opens Withdraw to Draft and Cancel activation, with the same dialogs and actions as the detail page. A cancelled activation keeps a Cancelled row (0 of 200, Cancelled 12 Oct, ₦200,000 refunded to iQLY credit) that opens the cancelled page: Cancelled pill, no More menu, stages Draft, In review and Cancelled, Held for spots ₦0.00 with the refund under it, and Send it again, which puts A2 back in Draft and opens Review and pay.
A draft that was paid before opens Review and pay from the list, and Review and pay reads the state: a draft withdrawn to Draft shows the Withdrawn banner and Resubmit for review, with nothing to pay; otherwise the checkout card, with Pay with (iQLY credit or Paystack) when the credit covers the amount, and the matching button. Once the task is set, the builder header and breadcrumb show it instead of New activation.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 7 · Pay from iQLY credit, resubmit for free (references)
desktop/05-activations.description: Reference frames, outside the click-through, set the prototype state explicitly: Review and pay for a draft withdrawn to Draft (mode Withdrawn), Review and pay and Add money with iQLY credit to spend (mode After cancel), Payments after paying again from iQLY credit (mode Paid from credit) and Payments after adding money (mode Added money). The modes hold the values a script got by running the stored actions.

desktop/05-activations.title: Row 7 · Help requests
desktop/05-activations.description: WhatsApp-style (owner 18 Oct): chat list on the left (search, Open and Resolved pills, last message, time, unread count), conversation on the right with a pinned claim bar (Reject, Confirm and pay ₦500), proof and messages as bubbles and voice notes, system notes, quick replies and a composer. Sorted closes the chat with the payout as a system note; none open shows a welcome card with round shortcuts.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 1 · 15 Oct, shortlisting
desktop/06-judging.description: Contained style (owner, 17 Oct): grey canvas, one white panel, the entry in a grey block. The four steps are a stepper, not tabs: the current step is its icon in a ring (hover for what the step is), the others are dots (hover shows their icon, faded). One queue, one entry at a time. iQLY marks entries: lilac means suggested, amber means flagged; click a mark to read why. A person decides each one: Shortlist, Pass (read, not for the shortlist) or Not considering (spam, copies or off-brief, with a reason and Restore). The demo follows the sample data: shortlist Zobolicious (A1), pass Kola Kick after reading iQLY’s reason (A1n, A1b), set Best drink ever aside with a reason (A1p, A1pb, A1pr), land on Red Cap (A1q). Score and Rank stay locked until the shortlist is done.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 2 · 15 Oct, scoring
desktop/06-judging.description: Every judge scores the same 8 entries; each criterion folds to one line. By default nobody sees other judges’ scores until every judge has finished; the owner can change that and who may break ties in Judging settings (gear on Overview). The overview shows who has finished, never the scores, and follows Tolu’s save: 21 of 24 before, 22 of 24 after.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 3 · All 24 scores in
desktop/06-judging.description: The team table opens: team score is the average of the judges’ weighted scores. A gap of 4 points or more is marked Discuss and shows the score without each outlier; the marks fold away. Rank follows the team score and only tied rows drag. Break the tie (or a drag) asks who takes 3rd, shows each judge’s score for both, and needs a reason every judge can see. Undo reopens the tie; the Overview and Rank step remember the choice.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 4 · Keeping the tie
desktop/06-judging.description: Right: both share 3rd and each gets the full ₦150,000, so the brand tops up ₦150,000 when it publishes. Break the tie asks who takes 3rd, from the kept tie too. Left: the shortlist once all scores are in.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 5 · Setting on, not the default
desktop/06-judging.description: A judge sees the team’s scores as soon as they save their own. The overlay on the right is the settings dialog the gear opens.

desktop/06-judging.title: Row 6 · Contained, with extras
desktop/06-judging.description: The same contained style plus an iQLY side panel (X2) and round icon actions that show their label on hover (X1, X3). The main rows above use labelled buttons pinned in the reader head.

mobile/01-home-and-getting-around.title: Mobile row 1 · Home and getting around
mobile/01-home-and-getting-around.description: Home: greeting, "Needs you" as three photo cards in a sideways scroll (option A: full photo with a dark overlay and white text; option B, N01b: photo strip above plain text), the week’s figures as cards with illustrations, and "Stats for quants" (N08) for the full side-by-side comparison. Wallet: a card for iQLY credit, quick actions, escrow and paid-out tiles, illustrated recent rows. Lists split by pill filters (Exp/Chip, no "All"). N09 is the all-caught-up empty state.

mobile/02-quick-challenge.title: Mobile row 2 · Quick challenge
mobile/02-quick-challenge.description: Name, what to send, prize pool with room for submissions on a slider, winners (Top 1, Top 3 or a custom number split evenly), how long, then a clear "You pay" breakdown and Pay. Everything else is changed after saving the draft.

mobile/03-quick-poll.title: Mobile row 3 · Quick poll
mobile/03-quick-poll.description: Question, answers, tags or not, how long, send. Live results show votes and each answer’s share.

mobile/04-quick-activation-and-claims.title: Mobile row 4 · Quick activation and claims
mobile/04-quick-activation-and-claims.description: Task, the steps (each opens its own edit screen with the help line, pay and devices), how steps are confirmed, spots, pay. Claims confirm one at a time with a playable proof and an undo snackbar.

mobile/05-judging.title: Mobile row 5 · Judging on the go
mobile/05-judging.description: Overview with progress and illustrated stages; entries as a swipeable card stack you can scroll inside, with round Not considering, Shortlist and Pass buttons; iQLY’s reason in a sheet; who has scored as judge avatars beside each entry (N49, dashed circle means not yet); one criterion per score screen; team scores as a podium; winners as cards; tie and publish in sheets.

mobile/06-help-requests.title: Mobile row 6 · Help requests on an activation
mobile/06-help-requests.description: Built like a WhatsApp chat. The list shows each contributor with their last message, time and unread count, under Open and Resolved pills. The chat has a pinned bar (claim waiting, ₦500 in escrow, Confirm and pay), their proof and message as bubbles and voice notes, system notes for dates and iQLY support, quick replies and a composer. Sorted shows the payout as a system note and closes the chat. Reached from Claims ("Help · 2"). Desktop versions sit in the Activations section.
